headline: Generative models infer single-cell dynamics, transitions and perturbation responses
label: Single Cell Representation And Dynamics
summary: Growing multimodal, spatial and time-resolved single-cell datasets demand models that jointly infer cell states, dynamics and perturbation responses.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned, structured representations of single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data used to recover dynamics and perturbation responses. Dynamics methods include kinetic-free RNA velocity from snapshot data (VelOT), Markov transition generators for unpaired time series (scMTG), Schrödinger bridges over endpoint-only transitions (FreeBridge), and physics-informed velocity coupled to gene regulatory networks (GRNvelo). Perturbation prediction appears in OCOO-T and VitaGRN, while HoloCell pretrains a foundation model on about 468M profiles. Spatial trajectory inference (StPedf) and mechanistic inference from multimodal counts (PRIME) are also represented. What is new is explicit interpretable counterfactual structure: scCBGM uses concept bottlenecks for counterfactual editing of scRNA-seq profiles, and Cellina applies supervised disentanglement to tissue graphs.
